title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. k is a field of characteristic 0, (X,x) is a curve of type (g,ν) with a point x, and M_{g,ν} is the moduli stack with universal curve 𝔛_{g,ν} → M_{g,ν}. On the previous page Grothendieck saw a problem. If k is algebraically closed, the profinite torsor P_{X,x} cannot recover (X,x): its automorphism group M_{X,x} has the cardinality of the continuum, while Aut(X,x) over k is finite. His remedy is to write k = lim K_i as a filtered union of finitely generated subfields; any structure (X,x) is 'defined over K_i for i large'.

On this page he fixes such a K = K_i and lets K̄ be the algebraic closure of K inside k. Diagram (7) is the tower of base changes of the universal curve and the moduli stack along Q → K → K̄ → k: 𝔛_{g,ν} over M_{g,ν} over the base field. The marginal remark notes that the extension K̄ ⊂ k (algebraically closed to algebraically closed, characteristic 0) is 'homotopically trivial', i.e. it does not change geometric étale fundamental groups. This is the invariance of π1 under extension of algebraically closed base fields in characteristic 0.

The datum (X,x) defined over K is a K-rational section x of 𝔛_{g,ν,K} → Spec K. Its image is a section ξ of M_{g,ν,K} → Spec K (the moduli point), and the k-sections are obtained by base change. He then defines (8):
- M_{X,x,K} = π1(𝔛_{g,ν,K}, x);
- N_{X,x,K} = π1(M_{g,ν,K}, ξ);
- Γ_{K̄|K} = Gal(K̄/K) = π1(Spec K).

The next page writes the resulting diagram (9). It has two short exact sequences: 1 → 𝔊_{X,x} → M_{X,x,K} → Γ_K → 1 and 1 → T̂ → N_{X,x,K} → Γ_K → 1. Here T̂ is the profinite Teichmüller (mapping class) group, i.e. the geometric π1 of the moduli stack. 𝔊 is the geometric π1 of the universal curve, an extension of T̂ by Π_X = π1(X). Both sequences are split by the sections x and ξ, giving an outer, then actual, Galois action.

He remarks that this K-situation is merely the pullback, along Γ_K → Γ_Q, of the absolute situation (1) over Q. The aim is to understand the 'Galois types' of curves over finitely generated fields: the anabelian set-up in which a finitely generated base field replaces an algebraically closed one, so that the Galois action can rigidify the torsor.
errors: No mathematical error. The page is set-up only; nothing is proved yet. The previous page's own note (NB on the next page) admits the K-rationality of (X,x) has not yet been used, so the construction so far is formal.

The claim that K̄ ⊂ k is 'homotopically trivial' is correct for geometric étale π1 in characteristic 0 (and for the profinite fundamental group of the moduli stack). He states it without justification.

ideas.what: Reduce from an arbitrary (e.g. algebraically closed) base field to a finitely generated one, so that profinite π1 data with Galois action could determine the curve. The motivation is that over an algebraically closed field the torsor has continuum-many automorphisms against finitely many automorphisms of (X,x).
ideas.modern_name: Anabelian geometry over finitely generated fields (Grothendieck's anabelian conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983; Esquisse 1984); proved by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (27 June 1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984); both printed in Schneps–Lochak, Geometric Galois Actions 1 (1997)

ideas.what: Tower of base changes of the universal curve and moduli stack, with π1 of moduli stack and universal curve over K forming extensions of Gal(K̄/K) by the profinite Teichmüller group and its extension by π1(X). The section given by a rational point gives a Galois action.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic fundamental group of M_{g,n} / Galois action on profinite mapping class groups (Teichmüller tower)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto, Oda, Schneps–Lochak

ideas.what: Invariance of geometric étale π1 under extension of algebraically closed fields in characteristic 0
ideas.modern_name: Base change invariance of étale fundamental group

ideas.what: The K-situation is the pullback of the absolute Q-extension along Γ_K → Γ_Q
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of group extensions / base change of the fundamental exact sequence

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a preparatory step that sets up notation for π1 of the universal curve and moduli stack over a finitely generated field. This framework is exactly what Grothendieck laid out in the 1983 Faltings letter and the Esquisse, so nothing appears new.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the reading 'de comprendre la configuration modulaire concrète' is uncertain; the image suggests something like 'd'exprimer la configuration ...' before 'des types "galoisiens" que l'on espère'.
In (8) the base point of π1(Spec K, ·) is written in the image roughly as 'k̄' (or k), effectively a geometric point via K̄ ⊂ k; the transcription's '\bar k' is plausible.

The first-row and middle-row objects in diagram (7) are 𝔛_{g,ν} (fraktur X) and M_{g,ν}; the transcription is correct. The dashed arrows go from K to M_{g,ν K} and 𝔛_{g,ν K}, representing the sections ξ and x.
The marginal note under K̄ — k reads 'au pt de vue homotopique, cette extension est de nature triviale', as transcribed.
